sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by award dated 29.09.2023 passed by 24th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in MACC No.308/2022 for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: 24th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that learned Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income on lower side whereas on the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.8800/-.
Therefore, Tribunal should have determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.8800/- per month.

Further, it is also urged that Tribunal has awarded Rs.44,000/- under the head of consortium only for appellant No.1 and it has not been awarded any consortium to remaining appellants whereas all the appellants are entitled to receive consortium at the rate of Rs.44,000/-.
On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
3. Learned counsel for respondent/insurance company submits that amount awarded by the tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
Appeal be dismissed.

4. I have heard leaned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
5. So far as income of deceased is concerned, on the date of accident, minimum wages of on unskilled labour were Rs.8800/- per month.
Therefore, deceased's monthly income is determined as Rs.8800/- per month.
6. In view of age of deceased, on the date of accident, 25% is to be added as future prospect and looking to the number of dependents  th is to deducted for personal and living expenses.
Having regard to age of deceased, multiplier of 14 is to be applied.
Further, appellants No.2, 3 and 4, being daughters of the deceased, they are also entitled to receive consortium at the rate of Rs.44,000/-.
Further, appellants are also received Rs.33,000/- for funereal/loss of estate and Rs.46,602/- for medical expenses.

7. In view of above, compensation awarded by the tribunal is recalculated as under:
 S. N. HEADS COM  1. Monthly Income of the deceased- (A ) Rs.8,800/
 2.

Monthly Income after adding future  Prospects-(B) Rs.11,000  { Future Prospects = 25% of monthly  income}
3. Personal & living expenses of the deceased 1/4 4.

Annual loss of dependency-(monthly loss of Rs.8,250/-
dependency x 12)
5.

Annual loss of dependency x 14 Rs.13,86,000/-
Multiplier) -(C)

6. Compensation for loss of Rs.1,76,000/-
spousal/parental/filial consortium-(D)
7. Compensation for loss of estate-(E) Rs.16,500/-
8. Compensation towards funeral expenses-(F) Rs.16,500/-
9.

Medical Expenses-(G) Rs.46,602/-
10.

TOTAL COMPENSATION- Rs.16,41,602/-
Smt. Neetu vs Gaurav Raikwar on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19662562/
2 {C+D+E+F+G=H}

11. Total Compensation awarded by the Rs.14,54,470/-
Tribunal-(I)
12. ACTUAL ENHANCEMENT-(H-I=J) Rs.1,87,132/-
8.
Appellants are entitled to receive enhanced amount of Rs.1,87,132/-.
Enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the tribunal.
Other findings of Tribunal shall remain intact.
9. Appellants shall not be entitled to receive interest on enhanced amount for period of 131 days.
10. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellants is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE sm Smt. Neetu vs Gaurav Raikwar on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19662562/
